Details of the scenario and retrofit measures in the activity have been developed using sample data that is representative of industry norms. The outcomes of the activity can vary widely based on how the participants’ interests and priorities influence the package of retrofit options they select. The building has had minimal energy improvements implemented over the years, and many systems are at end of life. The building is located in climate zone 4A, which is characterized by warm humid summers and cold winters (such as Washington, DC). Cooling is provided by an electric chiller and natural gas heating is provided by the original boiler that makes 180°F hot water. Hot and cold water is circulated to the building zones to a conventional variable air volume (VAV) system with reheat. Lighting is provided by T8 fluorescent lamps that were installed in the late 1990’s. The roof has been replaced once in 2005. Utility data has been collected from the building and logged over several years (an important first step in reducing loads) and it has been determined that the site EUI is 81 kBtu/ft2 annually. This is similar to buildings of this vintage and approximately twice the energy use of a building built to current practices. Please note that office buildings designed to achieve stringent energy goals can often operate around 20 kBtu/ft2.
